title: Burnout misread as career confusion
persona: 29-year-old staff backend engineer in Bengaluru running on 5 hours of sleep and late US-overlap calls

answers.questionText: How do you feel about your work right now?
answers.text: Drained

answers.questionText: When was the last time you lost track of time? What were you doing?
answers.text: Three months ago at my grandmother's house in Mysuru, pruning jasmine vines in the courtyard for two quiet hours with my phone switched off.

answers.questionText: What do people come to you for? Do you enjoy being that person?
answers.text: Production incidents at 11pm and calming panicked junior engineers. I used to like feeling indispensable, now my shoulders ache the moment Slack chimes.

answers.questionText: Describe a real Tuesday. Not ideal. Real.
answers.text: Wake up tired at 8:30 after a midnight US sync, skip breakfast, 7 hours of architecture reviews and incident postmortems, dinner at 10pm, stare at job boards wondering if I am in burnout or in the wrong field.

answers.questionText: What would you change if it were easy?
answers.text: Sleep nine uninterrupted hours for two weeks straight without anyone expecting me to rescue a release.

answers.questionText: Welcome back. Yesterday I left you with this: "Every change you wished for was about sleep and silence, not a new job. What if your career isn't broken — just your Tuesday?" Before we start, did anything surface overnight? Even something small.
answers.text: I noticed I felt guilty even typing 'sleep nine hours', as if rest has to be justified by a medical emergency.

answers.questionText: Think about the last three times you had genuine fun. What were you doing?
answers.text: Walking around Sankey Tank at sunrise, making filter coffee and dosas slowly on a rainy Saturday, playing carrom with my cousins during Pongal.

answers.questionText: Two projects: A is structured, B is open-ended. Which one lights you up?
answers.text: A is structured

answers.questionText: What counts as fun at work? Be specific.
answers.text: Designing one clean database migration in quiet morning hours when nobody interrupts me for three hours.

answers.questionText: What activities outside work make you feel most alive?
answers.text: Long morning walks under trees, swimming laps, cooking warm food without rushing.

answers.questionText: When you compare quiet morning database work with 11pm incident rescues, what shifted in how your week is set up?
answers.text: I never said no when they added the US-overlap squad on top of my India team, because my parents worked 14-hour days their whole lives and complaining felt weak.

answers.questionText: Welcome back. Yesterday I left you with this: "I notice you treat rest as something only earned through collapse. Where did that rule begin?" Before we start, did anything surface overnight? Even something small.
answers.text: Remembered my dad working through fevers and how proud everyone was of his stamina. I copied his schedule even though nobody asked me to.

answers.questionText: Which world (school, work, social) felt most like you? Which was the biggest performance?
answers.text: Quiet morning coding with two teammates feels like me. Pretending in all-hands meetings that 11pm calls are 'exciting global ownership' is a total performance.

answers.questionText: If you could be honest with everyone for one day, with zero consequences, what would you say, and to whom?
answers.text: I would tell my engineering director that I actually love backend craft, and my body is completely out of fuel from carrying two time zones.

answers.questionText: When you get dressed, are you dressing as who you are, or who you're creating?
answers.text: Mostly throwing on whatever clean t-shirt is nearest because I have zero energy left for anything else.

answers.questionText: Who would you still talk to if you lived in total isolation? Why them?
answers.text: My partner Ananya and my grandmother. Neither of them expects me to fix anything when I sit down.

answers.questionText: What do you imagine happens if you stop performing tireless availability after 7pm?
answers.text: Honestly, another lead in Seattle would probably pick up the night rotation within a week, and only my own pride would sting for five minutes.

answers.questionText: If nobody could judge you, what would you stop doing tomorrow?
answers.text: Keeping PagerDuty and Slack notifications unmuted on my nightstand.

answers.questionText: When was the last time you felt like yourself?
answers.text: Walking around Sankey Tank last month when my phone battery died and I couldn't check messages.

answers.questionText: Welcome back. Yesterday I left you with this: "You actually like the craft — you're just doing it across two time zones on an empty tank. What changes if you rest before you quit?" Before we start, did anything surface overnight? Even something small.
answers.text: Turned off Slack notifications at 8pm last night and felt weird relief instead of panic.

answers.questionText: Rank these: autonomy, mastery, impact, recognition, belonging.
answers.text: 1. mastery, 2. autonomy, 3. belonging, 4. impact, 5. recognition

answers.questionText: Look at how you spent last week. Does it match your ranking?
answers.text: No. I ranked autonomy second and recognition last, yet I gave away every evening to look like the heroic always-online lead.

answers.questionText: Imagine being privately, quietly proud five years from now. First image. Don't think.
answers.text: Finishing deep technical work by 5:30pm, swimming before dinner, cooking with Ananya without checking a laptop.

answers.questionText: Does prestige feel good, or just useful?
answers.text: Useful on a resume, completely useless at 11:30pm when my eyes burn.

answers.questionText: Your five-year pride image ends work at 5:30pm for a swim, while last week ran past midnight. What sits between the two?
answers.text: Equating rest with slacking off, and never taking the two weeks of accrued leave sitting untouched in HR.

answers.questionText: Welcome back. Yesterday I left you with this: "If the way you spent last week was a statement of your values, what would it say?" Before we start, did anything surface overnight? Even something small.
answers.text: I don't actually want to abandon backend engineering at all. I just need to stop running on fumes first.

answers.questionText: What would you do for free that people would eventually pay for?
answers.text: Untangling slow distributed systems calmly with a small team during humane daytime hours.

answers.questionText: What's the one move with low downside and huge upside that you've been avoiding?
answers.text: Taking my two weeks of saved leave next month and handing the US night rotation to the Seattle lead.

answers.questionText: Describe your ideal Monday morning. First three hours. Specific.
answers.text: Wake naturally at 6:30, walk around Sankey Tank in cool air, filter coffee with Ananya, open code at 9:30 with rested eyes.

answers.questionText: What would you bet on? Not the safe bet. The real one.
answers.text: Betting that sustainable daytime mastery lasts longer than late-night heroics.

answers.questionText: What's the one thing you know you need to do but haven't done yet?
answers.text: Submit two weeks of leave and end my US-overlap calls before making any big career jump.

answers.questionText: In your own words, name your top 3 priorities right now, and one small next step for each.
answers.text:
1. Priority: Recover sleep and physical energy — Next step: Put my phone in the living room at 8:30pm tonight.
2. Priority: End two-timezone overload — Next step: Message my director tomorrow to hand off the 11pm US sync.
3. Priority: Take real rest before judging my field — Next step: Block 10 days of accrued leave in Mysuru next month.

bridges.text: Every change you wished for was about sleep and silence, not a new job. What if your career isn't broken — just your Tuesday?
I notice you treat rest as something only earned through collapse. Where did that rule begin?
You actually like the craft — you're just doing it across two time zones on an empty tank. What changes if you rest before you quit?
If the way you spent last week was a statement of your values, what would it say?
What happens to your career fog once you are no longer answering it on five hours of sleep?
